A VPN (virtual private network) is a service that sends your internet traffic through a protected, private route before it reaches the website or app you're using.

When you switch it on, your phone or laptop makes an encrypted link to a machine run by the VPN company. Your traffic goes through that link, so your internet provider or anyone sharing your Wi-Fi sees scrambled data instead of what you're doing. The websites you visit see the VPN's address, not yours.

People use VPNs on public Wi-Fi, to reach office systems from home, or to appear in another country. A VPN doesn't make you fully anonymous, though. The VPN company can still see your activity, so pick one you trust.

VPN (virtual private network) ek private raasta hai, jisse aapka internet data pehle surakshit tareeke se guzarta hai aur phir website ya app tak pahunchta hai.

Jab aap VPN on karte hain, to aapka phone ya laptop VPN company ke computer se ek encrypted connection bana leta hai. Aapka internet provider ya same Wi-Fi use karne wale log sirf scrambled data dekhte hain, yeh nahi ki aap kya kar rahe hain. Website ko aapka nahi, VPN ka address dikhta hai.

Log VPN ka use public Wi-Fi par, ghar se office ke system tak pahunchne ke liye, ya doosre desh ka content dekhne ke liye karte hain. Lekin VPN aapko poori tarah anonymous nahi banata, kyunki VPN company aapki activity dekh sakti hai. Isliye bharosemand VPN hi chunein.
